notes: The 'Server ab 2,45 EUR' banner is the entry rung of four ladders and none of them is 8 GiB. The EUR 2.45 plan is 1 vCPU / 2 GiB / 20 GB / 5 TB in Frankfurt. The 8 GiB shapes are EUR 3.95 on the 2026-Sale ladder and EUR 5.99 on the Xeon ladder, both marked 'Ausverkauft'. Twenty-one of twenty-four rungs across the four KVM pages are sold out; three Ryzen GEN 2 rungs say 'Jetzt konfigurieren'. The buyable 4 GiB row is the one priced here, at EUR 3.95 = USD 4.42 with 10 TB of traffic, which is the largest transfer allowance of any sub-USD-5 row found. EUR converted at 1.1193 (ECB reference 2026-10-23). No card hold is stated anywhere. Two things remain open: the rails actually offered at balance top-up (login wall at /cp/credit/add), and whether a debit or prepaid card is accepted (only 'Kreditkarte' is named). The public order pages rendered a signed-in session string and their price summary did not reconcile with the product-page price, so the absolute figure on those pages was not used; only their structural text was, and it agreed across two pages.

extras.price_arithmetic: EUR 3.95 a month, VAT inclusive, billed monthly, prepaid; 3.95 x 1.1193 USD/EUR (ECB reference rate for 2026-10-23, read 2026-10-24) = USD 4.42 a month. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same number.
extras.renewal_note: no term discount and no first-term promo: every card reads 'Monatlich' with no strike-through price, and the order summary prints a 'Verlängerungsbetrag (30 Tage)' equal to the amount due today, so the renewal is the same monthly figure. The order page also describes the price as 'dauerhaft' (permanent).
extras.promo: the 2026-Sale page is named as a sale but states no end date and no post-sale price; the Ryzen ladder is not labelled a sale at all. The sale is capacity-limited, not time-limited: stock is released again when a server lapses, per the vendor's stock page.

session_cap.note: none; it is a VPS. The server is locked at expiry and deleted 5 days later, so an unattended lapse destroys the disk

benchmark.note: Ryzen 9 5950X at 3.39 GHz. One vCPU at $2.82 that outruns every 2 and 4 vCPU x86 row here on single core except Aeza.

confidence_note: every price, shape, traffic term and stock state below was read from the vendor's own pages as raw HTML; the text extractor drops the plan-to-price mapping, so the prices were parsed from the card markup. Prices are stated VAT-inclusive on the page; the order form's tax-country list includes '0% - Rest of the World / Outside EU', so a non-EU buyer may be charged less than the figure recorded here, and that net price is not published. No card hold is stated anywhere; the top-up page where a card would be charged is behind a login wall.
